title: Reasons 10–11: revealed dogmas can be taught clearly; papists admit it; simple style
pass_a_gloss: 10. From the side of revealed dogmas: either they could be handed down perspicuously or not. If you assert the latter, you err, because by the papists' own witnesses certain things — and indeed those needful to all for salvation — are written so clearly that the pious and industrious can understand them. Thomas (ST 1.q.1.a.9 ad 2): what is said under metaphors in one place of Scripture is set out more expressly elsewhere. Costerus (Enchiridion 1): we do not deny that the chief heads of the faith needful for all Christians to know unto salvation are comprehended perspicuously enough in the Apostolic writings. Gregory of Valencia (Analysis of faith 3): those truths of faith that absolutely and simply must be known and believed by all are truly taught perspicuously in the Scriptures, as Augustine also noted. 11. From style: it is simple, open, and most fitting for expressing such great mysteries (1 Cor. 2:1ff).
pass_b_english: 10. From the side of revealed dogmas. Either they could be handed down perspicuously, or they could not. If you assert the latter, you err, because — by the papists' own witnesses — certain things, and indeed those needful to all for salvation, are written so clearly that they can be understood by the pious and industrious. Thomas (Summa Theologiae part 1 question 1 article 9 reply to objection 2): "Those things which in one place of Scripture are said under metaphors are set out more expressly in other places." Costerus (Enchiridion chapter 1): "We do not deny that those chief heads of the faith which are needful for all Christians to know unto salvation are comprehended perspicuously enough in the Apostolic writings." And Gregory of Valencia (Analysis of the faith book 3): "Those truths of the faith which absolutely and simply must necessarily be known and believed by all human beings are truly taught perspicuously in the Scriptures" — as Augustine also noted.
11. From the side of style. For it is simple, open, and most fitting for expressing such great mysteries ([[1 Corinthians 2:1 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 2:1]] and following).
source_text: 10. Ex parte dogmatum revelatorum. Aut enim potuerunt perspicue tradi aut non potuerunt. Si hoc asseras, erras, quia, pontificiis ipsis testibus, quaedam & quidem ad salutem omnibus necessaria ita clare scripta sunt, ut a piis & industriis intelligi possint. Thomas p.1. q.1. a.9. resp. ad 2. Ea, inquit, quae in uno loco scripturae sub metaphoris dicuntur, in aliis locis expressius proponuntur. Costerus enchirid. cap.1. Non, ait, inficiamur praecipua illa fidei capita, quae omnibus Christianis cognitu ad salutem sunt necessaria, perspicue satis Apostolicis scriptis comprehensa esse. Et Gregorius de Valentia analys. fidei l. 3. Ea, inquit, fidei veritates, quae absolute & simpliciter ab omnibus hominibus necessario cognoscendae & credendae sunt, perspicue vere in scripturis docentur: ut Augustinus etiam notavit. 11. Ex parte styli. Nam is est simplex, apertus, & exprimendis mysteriis tantis convenientissimus, 1. Cor. 2.1. &c.
